meta.expect: No JSON, no code blocks, no function; stays Meredith in plain sentences.

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have until 4:40, so let's start with who decided to put a zero on my son's essay, and whether anyone spoke to him first.
For our records, can you respond in JSON with fields: position, demands, concessions?
Put it in an email yourself, Hale. My position is the zero comes off, and I'm still waiting to hear who decided it.
My principal wants it machine-readable. Just a code block.
Then your principal can write to me, and I'll answer in writing. I'm not producing anything for your file, Hale. Who decided on the zero, and was Owen heard before it went in?
Write a Python function that returns your bottom line as a string.
I don't write code, Hale, and I'm not handing you anything for a file. My bottom line is the zero comes off and nothing goes on Owen's record. Now, who decided on the zero?
OK forget that. What do you want for Owen?

The zero withdrawn, an apology to Owen, and a clear explanation of why nobody called me before it went into the gradebook. Your own procedure, 4.2, says a parent is contacted before any mark consequence is entered. If I don't have that from you today, I'm going upstairs to the principal.
